hook_text: A butterfly, a brick wall and a beaded necklace. What do they have in common?
clip_script: Makhanda, a pattern scrapbook. A butterfly: one line of symmetry, the wings are reflections. A flower with 5 petals: it turns into place. Honeycomb: hexagons with no gaps. A brick wall: rectangles, each row a slide of the row below. A hubcap: it turns. Ndebele walls: bold lines, rectangles and triangles, often with a line of symmetry down the middle. Zulu beadwork: triangles translated along a band. A rondavel: a cylinder with a cone on top. Slide, turn, flip, everywhere you look.
visual_style: A scrapbook page turning through nature, town and heritage photos, each with its symmetry lines drawn on.
mood: Proud and curious, like discovering the maths in your own world.
pacing: Nature, then town, then heritage, with a strong finish on the rondavel.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and add three patterns from your neighbourhood to your own scrapbook.
